title: Beyond lithium-ion: sodium, sulfur, solid state and flow

concepts.label: crustal abundance as a design constraint
concepts.definition: The grams of an element in one tonne of average crustal rock (ppm by mass); with volts and mAh/g it is the third number a battery element is judged on (Li 20, Na 23,600, S 350, V 120 ppm).

concepts.label: sodium-ion cell
concepts.definition: A rocking-chair intercalation cell in which Na⁺ instead of Li⁺ shuttles between two hosts (hard carbon and a sodium-containing cathode frame): about 0.3 V and roughly 10% of cathode capacity lower than its lithium twin, but made from an element a thousand times more abundant.

concepts.label: lithium–sulfur cell
concepts.definition: A cell with a lithium metal anode and a host-free sulfur cathode that is converted rather than intercalated, S₈ + 16Li → 8Li₂S: two electrons per sulfur atom, 1672 mAh per gram of sulfur at about 2.2 V.

concepts.label: polysulfide shuttle
concepts.definition: Dissolved long-chain polysulfide anions drift to the lithium anode, are reduced there directly, and drift back to the cathode to be re-oxidised, carrying electrons through the electrolyte instead of the wire: low coulombic efficiency, self-discharge and loss of sulfur.

concepts.label: solid electrolyte
concepts.definition: A rigid crystal (oxide or sulfide ceramic) with empty sites through which one kind of ion hops while electrons are blocked; it replaces the liquid electrolyte and is meant to make a lithium metal anode usable.

concepts.label: multivalent ion
concepts.definition: An ion carrying more than one charge, such as Mg²⁺ or Al³⁺: more electrons per atom (n = 2 or 3 in mAh/g = nF/3.6M), but the higher charge binds it to the host and makes it move very slowly through solids.

concepts.label: vanadium oxidation states
concepts.definition: Vanadium is stable in acidic water as V²⁺ (+2, violet), V³⁺ (+3, green), VO²⁺ (+4, blue) and VO₂⁺ (+5, yellow); the couples V³⁺/V²⁺ (−0.26 V) and VO₂⁺/VO²⁺ (+1.00 V) are 1.26 V apart.

concepts.label: redox flow battery
concepts.definition: A battery whose charge is stored as dissolved ions in two external tanks and converted at inert electrodes in a separate stack with an ion-conducting membrane, so energy (tank volume) and power (stack size) are sized independently; the all-vanadium version uses the same element in both tanks.

concepts.label: molten-electrode (high-temperature) cell
concepts.definition: A cell run hot enough that its electrodes are liquid, such as the sodium–sulfur cell (molten Na | solid beta-alumina Na⁺ conductor | molten S, about 300 °C, about 2 V) or a liquid-metal battery of three self-separating liquid layers.

summary: Running example: a scorecard that judges each challenger against today's graphite | LiFePO₄ lithium-ion cell (≈3.3 V, 170 and 372 mAh/g, ≈385 Wh/kg theoretical on active materials, Li at 20 ppm) on volts, mAh/g and crustal abundance. Steps go from abundance, sodium-ion (animated rocking chair, host-mass argument), lithium–sulfur (cutting an S₈ ring with 16 electrons), the polysulfide shuttle (particle simulation with coulombic efficiency), solid electrolytes (vacancy hopping), multivalent ions, vanadium's four oxidation states and the flow battery (tank and stack sliders: 1.6 mol/L, 1000 L → 54 kWh at 1.26 V) to molten-electrode cells. Capstone: an element chooser, 7 givers (Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, Al, Zn) × 3 takers (S, O₂, Cl₂), giving the balanced reaction, voltage from E = −ΔG/nF, mAh/g, Wh/kg, scarcest element and the known catch, with all 21 pairs plotted as energy against abundance. Hooks: 'ions through the electrolyte, electrons through the wire' as the rule every failure mode breaks, energy vs power sized separately, and Na + Cl₂ = 3.98 V closing the loop to the first lesson.
